'''Homi Suwa Jugosho Shrine''' (穂見諏訪十五所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Hokuto, Yamanashi|ar|هوكوتو (ياماناشي)|azb|هوکوتو، یاماناشی|ca|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|ce|Хокуто (Яманаси)|ceb|Hokuto-shi (distrito sa Hapon, Yamanashi-ken)|cs|Hokuto (Jamanaši)|de|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|eo|Hokuto|es|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|fa|هوکوتو، یاماناشی|fi|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|fr|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|gl|Hokuto, Yamanashi|hy|Հոկուտո (Յամանասի)|id|Hokuto, Yamanashi|it|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|ja|北杜市|ko|호쿠토시 (야마나시현)|lb|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|mzn|هوکوتو، یاماناشی|nl|Hokuto (Yamanashi)|pl|Hokuto (Honsiu)|pt|Hokuto|ro|Hokuto, Yamanashi|ru|Хокуто (Яманаси)|sr|Хокуто|sv|Hokuto, Yamanashi|tg|Ҳокуто|tl|Hokuto, Yamanashi|tr|Hokuto, Yamanashi|tt|Хокуто (Яманаси)|uk|Хокуто (Яманасі)|ur|ہوکوٹو، یاماناشی|vi|Hokuto, Yamanashi|war|Hokuto, Yamanashi|zh|北杜市|zh_classical|北杜市|zh_min_nan|Hokuto-chhī|zh_yue|北杜|qid=Q825272|lt=Hokuto, Yamanashi}}, Nagasaka Town, Kamijo Miyakubo 1461, in {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|qid=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}}. The shrine was previously classified as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度}}. Its main shrine, Tubokayu ritual, and a large zelkova tree on its grounds are designated as city cultural assets.<ref name="HokutoCityOverview2014">{{Cite book|author=Hokuto City |title=Hokuto City Overview 2014 |publisher=Hokuto City |date=2014}}</ref> The ''Kai Kokushi'' records the shrine’s estate as "4 koku and 7 to of stamped land, shrine grounds, mountain forest, and 3 tan and 2 se of paddies."<ref>''Kai Kokushi,'' Vol. 3. Yūzankaku, 1982, p. 97.</ref>

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines multiple deities due to numerous amalgamations, with three significant kami:
* {{ill|Ukemochi|en|Ukemochi|qid=Q2280323|lt=Ukemochi}}
* {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391}}
* {{ill|Five Deities of Heaven, Earth, and Man|ja|天地人五行神|qid=Q140446096}}

== History ==
=== Amalgamation of Shrines ===
Homi Suwa Jugosho Shrine was formed by the amalgamation of multiple shrines. It is speculated to have been founded in the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan era}}, 6th year (864). The ''Engishiki'' completed in {{ill|913|en|913|qid=Q24860|lt=913}} mentions a "Homi Shrine in Kai Province," identifying it as an {{ill|Ancient shrine|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Nagasaka Homeland |publisher=Nagasaka Town Local Studies Association |date=2008 |pages=11–15}}</ref>

In the 13th century, a shrine official was established, and the monk Ryūzō resided there, practicing esoteric rites and reportedly engaging in doctrinal debates with {{ill|Nichiren|Nichiren|Nichiren|qid=Q31147812=simple|lt=Nichiren}}. By 1275, the {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Five Elements (Wuxing)}} (Five Elements theory) influenced the shrine's practices.

During the {{ill|Tenmon|ja|天文|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q21096812}} famine (1534–1547), {{ill|Takeda Nobutora|en|Takeda Nobutora|qid=Q1192628|lt=Takeda Nobutora}} ordered the Tubokayu ritual to ensure agricultural prosperity. The shrine's current amalgamated form dates to this period.

== Architecture and Grounds ==
The shrine covers 848 tsubo. A {{ill|Natural monument|en|Natural monument|qid=Q23790|lt=natural monument}} zelkova tree is located within the shrine grounds, alongside an ancient main shrine reconstructed in the Edo period.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Kyohoku Shrine Chronicle |publisher=Kyohoku Shrine Council |date=1962}}</ref>

== Rituals ==
=== Tubokayu Ritual ===
The shrine’s Tubokayu divination ritual has been practiced since the 16th century, using rice porridge to predict agricultural outcomes.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Nagasaka Homeland |publisher=Nagasaka Town Local Studies Association |date=1988 |pages=62–66}}</ref>

== Cultural Assets ==
Three items are designated as cultural assets:
* Main Shrine: Rebuilt in the Edo period.
* Sacred Zelkova Tree: Estimated to be over 700 years old.
* Tubokayu Ritual: A unique divination practice carried out during {{ill|First Full Moon Festival|en|First Full Moon Festival|qid=Q13423452|lt=Koshogatsu}}.
